note: Thesis: AI compute demand is accelerating the adoption of advanced nodes, advanced packaging and optical interconnect (CPO / silicon photonics), and pulling demand through to foundry, packaging, memory and optics supply chains. Stance is relative to this thesis: supports = backs a link in the chain (demand growth, capacity expansion and plans, CPO production and shipments, laser and silicon-photonics orders); contradicts = weakens it (capacity bottlenecks slowing adoption, qualification cycles, fewer lasers per unit, a later CPO ramp, pluggable and integrated-laser routes coexisting, export controls limiting demand from China); neutral = background only (definitions, supply-chain disclosures, revenue or sales levels without a direction, research motivation). For export controls, easing exports to China or allies is supports; tightening or keeping restrictions is contradicts. Each excerpt reflects its own date, not the state in October 2026; research-firm excerpts (TrendForce, Third Bridge) are forecasts and judgments at publication, not realized outcomes. Revenue share is not capacity share, and HPC is not the same as AI.
